lessons.title: What the game is about
lessons.objective: You can say in one sentence how a team wins.

payload.prompt: How many points is a touchdown worth?

explanation.correct: Six points for the touchdown, then the team gets one or two more points with the extra point or two-point try. That is why fans cheer a touchdown.
explanation.incorrect: A touchdown is six points by itself. The kick that comes after is the extra point. If the team tries from the 2-yard line instead, that is two more points.
explanation.sayThisLine: That is six, then they get to shoot for one or two more.

payload.prompt: Tap the end zone.

explanation.correct: Those are the end zones, 10 yards deep at each end. Get the ball there and it is six points.
explanation.incorrect: The end zones are the striped areas at the ends of the field, past the goal line. That is touchdown territory.
explanation.sayThisLine: Get into the end zone and it is a touchdown.

payload.prompt: Which team is on offense?

options.text: The one guarding the end zone

explanation.correct: The offense has the ball and tries to score. The defense does not have it and tries to stop them. One team is always on each side.
explanation.incorrect: Possession is who has the ball. That team is the offense. The other team is on defense.
explanation.sayThisLine: Possession changed. Now they have the ball.

payload.prompt: Where can a team score a touchdown?

options.text: Only if the player runs it in
By running or catching the ball in the end zone

explanation.correct: A touchdown can happen on a run or a pass catch in the end zone. Either way, the ball just has to get there.
explanation.incorrect: A touchdown counts if the offense gets the ball into the end zone, whether they are running with it or catching a pass.
explanation.sayThisLine: Touchdown! Either running or catching.

payload.setting: Your friend says the team is close to scoring.
payload.theirLine: We are in the end zone!

replies.explanation: Correct. Get the ball into the end zone and it counts as a touchdown, which is six points.
Close. They scored a touchdown, so six points are on the board. Then the team gets to attempt an extra point kick or a two-point try.
Not quite. A touchdown is six, not ten. After a touchdown the team kicks for one more point (making it seven) or tries a two-point conversion.

lessons.title: The field and the line
lessons.objective: You can point to the end zone, yard lines and the line of scrimmage.

payload.prompt: Tap the line of scrimmage. Where the ball sits before the play.

explanation.correct: That is the line of scrimmage. Neither team can cross it until the snap. The offense lines up on one side, the defense on the other.
explanation.incorrect: The line of scrimmage is where the ball sits at the start of each play. It is an imaginary line that neither team can cross before the snap.
explanation.sayThisLine: Lined up at the line of scrimmage.

payload.prompt: The quarterback took a sack on the 40-yard line. That is good field _____ for the defense.

explanation.correct: Field position is where the ball sits. The closer to the other end zone, the fewer yards you need to score. A sack at midfield is good defense.
explanation.incorrect: You are looking for a word that describes where the ball sits on the field. Closer to the goal line is better field position for the offense.
explanation.sayThisLine: They pinned us deep. Rough field position.

payload.prompt: How far is the end zone from the line of scrimmage on a kickoff?

explanation.correct: The field is 100 yards long between the goal lines. Each end zone is 10 yards deep beyond that. So from one end zone to the other is 120 yards.
explanation.incorrect: The field between the goal lines is 100 yards. The end zones add 10 more yards at each end.
explanation.sayThisLine: Hundred yards between the goal lines.

payload.prompt: Now tap one of the end zones.

explanation.correct: That is an end zone. The team defending this end zone is trying to keep the ball out. The other team is trying to get the ball into this end zone to score.
explanation.incorrect: The end zones are the striped areas beyond the goal line. They are 10 yards deep.
explanation.sayThisLine: In the end zone for a touchdown.

lessons.title: Four downs
lessons.objective: You can explain what a down is and why fourth down matters.

payload.prompt: What does a first down give the offense?

explanation.correct: Gain 10 yards and the count resets: four fresh tries. That is why fans cheer a first down.
explanation.incorrect: A first down resets the offense to four tries at another 10 yards. It is not points or timeouts, just more time with the ball.
explanation.sayThisLine: They picked up the first down, so they keep the ball.

payload.prompt: The offense gets four _____ to advance 10 yards.

explanation.correct: The offense has four tries (downs) to gain 10 yards. If they do, they get four more. If they fail to gain 10, the other team gets the ball.
explanation.incorrect: A down is a play. The offense gets four of them to move the ball 10 yards.
explanation.sayThisLine: Fourth down, they have to go for it.

payload.prompt: Third and five. The running back gains five yards.

explanation.correct: They needed five yards and got five. That is a first down. The count resets to 1st and 10.
explanation.incorrect: Third and five means they need five yards. They got five, so that is a first down.
explanation.sayThisLine: Just enough for the first down.

payload.prompt: It is third and seven. What does that mean?

options.text: The offense has had two plays, needs seven more yards
The offense has seven chances to move the ball
It is the third quarter and the score is 7-0

explanation.correct: Third and seven means it is the third play of this set and they need seven yards to get a first down. If they fall short, it is fourth down and likely a punt or field goal.
explanation.incorrect: Third and seven: third play, seven yards needed. That is the down and distance.
explanation.sayThisLine: Third and seven, they have to throw.

payload.prompt: Why do fans care so much about fourth down?

options.text: It is usually the last chance to keep the ball
It is the hardest down to play

explanation.correct: Fourth down is the last try to gain 10 yards. If they do not make it, the other team gets the ball. So the team must decide: go for it, kick a field goal, or punt.
explanation.incorrect: Fourth down is crucial because it is the last chance in that sequence. Fail and possession flips.
explanation.sayThisLine: Fourth and goal, the pressure is on.

payload.setting: You are watching and hear someone say it is second and eight.
payload.theirLine: Second and eight means they did not get much on first down.

replies.text: Right, they need eight more yards.
replies.explanation: Correct. Second and eight: the second play, eight yards still needed. They gained two yards on the first play, so eight remain.
Correct. Second and eight is the second down of this set. They gained two yards on first, so eight yards remain to earn a first down.
No. Second and eight is about down and distance, not points. It means the second play and eight yards still needed.

lessons.title: Where is the first down?
lessons.objective: You can read the yellow line and say if they got the first down.

payload.prompt: The ball is at the yellow line. Did they get the first down?

explanation.correct: The yellow line is the first-down marker. If the ball reaches it or passes it, it is a first down. The chains measure it exactly if it is close.
explanation.incorrect: The yellow line shows where 10 yards ends. Reach or pass it and the offense gets a new set of downs.
explanation.sayThisLine: He got to the marker for the first down.

payload.prompt: Tap where the first-down marker is.

explanation.correct: That is the first-down marker (the yellow line on TV). If the ball gets there, the offense earns a new set of downs.
explanation.incorrect: The first-down marker shows where 10 yards ends from the original line of scrimmage.
explanation.sayThisLine: Right at the first-down marker.

payload.prompt: Second and three. The receiver gains four yards.

explanation.correct: Second and three means they need three yards. They got four, so they passed the marker. That is a first down.
explanation.incorrect: If they needed three and got four, they reached the marker. That counts as a first down.
explanation.sayThisLine: He got past the marker.

payload.prompt: Why do they use the chains on the sideline sometimes?

options.text: To measure if the ball is exactly at the first-down marker

explanation.correct: When a play is close to the first-down marker, the chains come out. They measure the exact 10 yards to see if it is a first down or not.
explanation.incorrect: The chains on the sideline are an official measuring tool. They show exactly where 10 yards ends.
explanation.sayThisLine: It is close, bring out the chains.

lessons.title: The clock
lessons.objective: You can say how long a game is and why it feels longer.

payload.prompt: How long are the four quarters of regulation in total minutes?

explanation.correct: Sixty minutes of playing time: four 15-minute quarters. In reality, games take about three hours because the clock stops often.
explanation.incorrect: The game is four quarters of 15 minutes each, so 60 minutes total. But with stoppages, it lasts about three hours.
explanation.sayThisLine: It is 60 minutes of play time, but the game lasts three hours.

payload.prompt: Why do games last about three hours when regulation is 60 minutes?

options.text: The clock stops for incompletions, out of bounds, and timeouts
They add extra time between quarters

explanation.correct: The clock stops after an incomplete pass, when the ball goes out of bounds, during timeouts, and for injuries or official reviews. So 60 minutes of playing time stretches across almost three hours.
explanation.incorrect: The clock does not run continuously like in soccer. It stops constantly, which is why games take longer than the 60 minutes of actual play.
explanation.sayThisLine: The clock stopped three times that quarter.

payload.prompt: What is the play clock and what happens if it runs out?

options.text: A 40-second countdown to snap the ball; if it hits zero, it is delay of game
The time between plays; if it runs out, the quarter ends
The time the quarterback has to throw before a sack

explanation.correct: The play clock counts down 40 seconds (or 25 after certain stoppages). If it hits zero before the snap, the offense is charged with delay of game, a five-yard penalty.
explanation.incorrect: The play clock is a 40-second timer that makes sure the offense snaps the ball. Run it out and it is a penalty.
explanation.sayThisLine: Snap it, the play clock is dying.

payload.prompt: The play clock just started at 40 seconds. Tap when the offense should snap the ball before delay of game.

explanation.correct: Good. If the offense snaps with a few seconds left, they avoid a delay of game penalty.
explanation.incorrect: The play clock runs 40 seconds. They need to snap before it hits zero.
explanation.sayThisLine: They got it off just in time.

payload.prompt: How many timeouts does each team get per half?

explanation.correct: Each team gets three timeouts per half (six total per game). They use them to stop the clock, draw up a play, or rest.
explanation.incorrect: Teams get three timeouts each half to stop the clock and regroup. Once they are used up, no more until the next half.
explanation.sayThisLine: He burned his last timeout to think.

lessons.title: How points happen
lessons.objective: You can add up a score from touchdowns, kicks and safeties.

payload.prompt: Match each score to its point value.

pairs.definition: Getting the ball into the end zone
Kicking the ball through the uprights
Tackling the offense in its own end zone

explanation.summary: Touchdowns are six. Field goals are three. An extra point kick is one. Two-point tries are two. A safety is two and you get the ball back.
explanation.sayThisLine: Touchdown, that is six, then the extra point.

payload.prompt: A kicker just made a 40-yard field goal. How many points is that?

explanation.correct: Three points for a field goal, no matter how far. A 40-yard kick is in range and makes it.
explanation.incorrect: Field goals are worth three points. The distance does not change the value, just the difficulty.
explanation.sayThisLine: That is three points for the field goal.

payload.prompt: After a touchdown, the team attempts an extra point. What is the most common extra point?

options.text: A kick from the 15-yard line for one point
A pass play from the 2-yard line for two points
A kick from the end zone for three points

explanation.correct: The extra point kick is the most common. The ball is snapped from the 15-yard line (a 33-yard kick). Make it and it is one point.
explanation.incorrect: After a touchdown, the team can kick for one or try from the 2-yard line for two. The kick is more common.
explanation.sayThisLine: Extra point is good, that is seven total.

payload.prompt: When might a team choose a two-point try over an extra point kick?

options.text: Late in the game when they need to catch up quickly
Never, the kick is always better

explanation.correct: Late in a game, if they are behind, a team might go for two to catch up faster. It is riskier (50-50 often) but worth two points instead of one if it works.
explanation.incorrect: Teams usually kick for one, but when trailing late, going for two is a gamble worth taking.
explanation.sayThisLine: They are going for two. Bold.

payload.prompt: Final score: touchdown and extra point, plus a field goal, plus a safety. Total?

explanation.correct: Touchdown (6) plus extra point (1) equals 7. Add a field goal (3) and you have 10. Add a safety (2) and the total is 12... wait, let me check: 6+1+3+2=12. Yes, 12 points.
explanation.incorrect: Add it up: touchdown (6) + extra point (1) + field goal (3) + safety (2) = 12 points.
explanation.sayThisLine: They scored 12 points that drive.

lessons.title: Giving the ball away
lessons.objective: You can say the difference between a fumble, an interception and a punt.

payload.prompt: Match the term to what it means.

pairs.definition: The offense loses the ball to the defense by interception or fumble
A pass caught by a defender before the receiver
The ball carrier drops the ball and either team can recover it
A kick on fourth down that gives the ball to the other team far downfield

distractorDefinitions: An incomplete pass on third down

explanation.summary: Interceptions and fumbles are turnovers. Punts are intentional and do not count as turnovers.
explanation.sayThisLine: Turnover on downs, they get the ball.

payload.prompt: A pass is thrown, and a linebacker jumps in front of the receiver and catches it. What is that?

explanation.correct: When a defender catches the pass, it is an interception. The defense takes over the ball and can run it back for a score.
explanation.incorrect: An interception is a pass caught by a defender. The defense takes over possession right there.
explanation.sayThisLine: He got picked off, the linebacker had it the whole way.

payload.prompt: The running back is hit hard and the ball pops out. A lineman falls on it.

explanation.correct: That is a fumble. The ball came loose and was recovered. If the defense recovered it, they get the ball.
explanation.incorrect: When a ball carrier loses the ball, that is a fumble. Either team can recover it.
explanation.sayThisLine: Fumble! Who has it?

payload.setting: She is frustrated after a turnover late in the game.
payload.theirLine: We had that turnover at the worst time.

replies.text: Yeah, we were driving and just gave it away.
replies.explanation: Right. A turnover ends the drive and flips possession. Late in the game, that is costly.

replies.text: Was it an interception or a fumble?
replies.explanation: Good question. Interception or fumble, both are turnovers. Either way, possession flips to the other team.
True, but turnovers change games. Late in a game, one turnover can be the difference between winning and losing.
